title_en: Ṭalaʿa al-Badru ʿAlaynā (The Full Moon Has Risen)
author: The people of Madinah
description_en: The historic welcome sung by the people of Madinah — by its women and children — as the Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ arrived in the radiant city during the Hijrah, descending over the northern pass known as Thaniyyāt al-Wadāʿ (The Passes of Farewell). Among the oldest, most poignant, and universally beloved anthems of devotion in Islamic history.
source_en: Traditional text sung upon the Prophet’s ﷺ arrival in Madinah, transmitted in classical sīrah and ḥadīth works (including al-Bayhaqī’s Dalāʾil al-Nubuwwah and Ibn Kathīr’s al-Bidāyah wa-al-Nihāyah). Classical traditionists record its singing upon his entry at Qubāʾ during the Hijrah (1 AH / 622 CE), as well as upon his triumphant return from the Expedition of Tabūk (9 AH / 630 CE). The English poetic rendering is original to this project.

sections.heading: The Welcome Song
sections.note: Sung at Qubāʾ on the outskirts of Madinah upon the arrival of the Prophet ﷺ during the Hijrah (Rabīʿ al-Awwal 1 AH / September 622 CE).

units.ar: طَلَعَ الْبَدْرُ عَلَيْنَا — مِنْ ثَنِيَّاتِ الْوَدَاعِ
units.en: The full moon has risen upon us — from the Passes of Farewell;

units.ar: وَجَبَ الشُّكْرُ عَلَيْنَا — مَا دَعَا لِلَّهِ دَاعِ
units.en: and thanks is owed from us — as long as a caller calls to Allah.

units.ar: أَيُّهَا الْمَبْعُوثُ فِينَا — جِئْتَ بِالْأَمْرِ الْمُطَاعِ
units.en: O you who were sent among us — you came with a command to be obeyed;

units.ar: جِئْتَ شَرَّفْتَ الْمَدِينَةَ — مَرْحَبًا يَا خَيْرَ دَاعٍ
units.en: you came and honoured Madinah — welcome, O best of callers.
